author: Roszczyk
title: Windows CC build fails with compiler/linker out-of-memory errors under high parallelism
signature: Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and linker fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) under high parallelism|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode
failed_jobs.symptom: MSVC cl.exe emits 'fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space' across dozens of unrelated template op_reference test files during parallel Release build

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_cc
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status-check job fails because Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode failed (no independent issue)

key_errors: C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\openvino\src\plugins\template\tests\functional\op_reference\convolution.cpp(233): fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space
C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.42.34433\include\filesystem(1312): fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space
C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.42.34433\include\vector(3886): fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space
root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation Release build compiles many large template-instantiation-heavy test files (src/plugins/template/tests/functional/op_reference/*.cpp) concurrently with a high parallel job count. Each cl.exe invocation for these heavily templated files (col2im.cpp, convolution.cpp, ctc_loss.cpp, deformable_convolution.cpp, etc.) consumes significant heap memory; when enough of them run in parallel on the same Windows runner, the compiler process exhausts available heap space and aborts with fatal error C1060. This is a resource-exhaustion/infrastructure condition caused by the combination of runner memory limits and build parallelism, not a defect in any specific source file - the same pattern has recurred 19 times since 2026-11-03.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI; requires a Windows runner with the same memory limits and ninja/msbuild parallelism (-j N) building the full Release + conditional-compilation configuration of ov_template_func_tests. Locally, building with a high parallel job count on a memory-constrained Windows machine can reproduce fatal error C1060.
recommended_actions: Reduce the parallel compile job count (-j / CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL / ninja -j) for the Windows Conditional Compilation workflow, especially for the template functional test target which contains many heavily templated op_reference files.

Consider splitting ov_template_func_tests into smaller translation units or reducing template instantiation depth in generator helpers (e.g., generateCol2ImParams, getContinuousIncreasingValue) to lower per-file compiler memory usage.
Evaluate moving to a Windows runner SKU with more available memory, or enable /Zm (increase compiler memory allocation limit) as a stopgap.
Add retry-with-reduced-parallelism logic to the Windows CC workflow so a single transient heap exhaustion does not fail the whole post-commit run.
prevention_strategies: Cap build parallelism relative to available runner memory, monitor Windows runner memory headroom during Release builds, and keep template-heavy test files from growing further without splitting them into smaller compilation units.
historical_context: This exact signature has been recorded 19 times in the post-commit pattern database since 2026-11-03 (pattern 80cfa127185fbf3e), consistently manifesting as compiler C1060 and/or linker LNK1102 out-of-memory errors on the Windows CC Release build under high parallelism. It is a well-known recurring infrastructure issue, not tied to any specific commit's code changes.
